tasks.notes: `_iso` (skills/ultralearn/scripts/census_many.py:104-110) calls `datetime.fromtimestamp` unguarded. The module's own docstring promises "an unreadable record costs its own columns, not the table", but an out-of-range `ts` in one run's `events.jsonl` (a value beyond year 9999, or negative past the platform's floor) raises OverflowError/OSError/ValueError out of `census_row` and aborts the whole census — every other run's row is lost with it. Every other read path in the file already degrades to the empty string. Not pinned by any Machine clause and not reachable from the fixtures, so advisory only.; unverified: `_is_wave_phase` (skills/ultralearn/scripts/census_many.py:263-266) counts `Depth-1 Leg` as a wave phase alongside `Wave*`. The Context's rule says only "first `Wave` phase ts", though the same Context does list `Depth-1 Leg` as the pre-#712 spelling of that phase, so the reading is lawful and it is disclosed in the function's docstring. No fixture carries a `Depth-1 Leg` event, so the branch is unexercised: deleting it leaves all 12 tests green, and on a pre-#712 run it silently changes `setup_min`/`wave_min` from the empty string to a number. What would settle it: a fourth fixture run whose log spells the phase `Depth-1 Leg`, asserting the two spans it produces.; `markdown_table` (skills/ultralearn/scripts/census_many.py:403-413) joins raw cell values with ` | ` without escaping a literal `|`. Every pinned column value is pipe-free, so no Machine clause or Proof leg is affected, but `--label run-101=lift|era` (M5 accepts arbitrary TEXT) emits a row with 32 cells and silently corrupts the M4 pipe table. Suggested fix: render each cell through a helper that replaces `|` with `\|` in `markdown_table` only (the CSV path is already quoted correctly by `csv.DictWriter`).

completenessFindings.detail: Task 2 (`skills/ultralearn/scripts/_readers.py:132` `released_versions`, consumed by `skills/ultralearn/scripts/merge_ledger.py:88`) — Claim slot, over-refusal in a truncated clone. The Claim is that the merge "turns away a finding stamped with a version this plugin never released". `released_versions()` returns `None` only when `release_timeline()` is exactly empty; the task's own Context names the other degraded case — "a one-row timeline in a depth-1 clone" — and that case yields a one-element frozenset, not `None`, so `merge_findings` would refuse every finding stamped with a genuinely released version other than that one row, silently counting them under `refused` rather than answering "cannot judge". This is inside the contract (M4 pins `None` on `()` only) and the merge is documented to run on the operator's full clone, so it does not block the merge, but the refusal rule's failure mode in a shallow clone is the opposite of fail-open and is worth an issue.
